title: useEffect Dependency Loop: Object Reference Churn vs Primitive URL Derivation
description: Trace how allocating { status: "open" } per render fails Object.is(), saturates HTTP connections with uncancelled GET /api/items requests, and triggers 429 rate limits.

steps.label: 1. Fresh Heap Allocation per Render (t = 0 ms)
steps.description: The filter component executes and builds const filter = { status: searchParams.get('status') ?? 'open' }. V8 allocates a brand-new object reference @0x7f1a04 on the heap.
steps.codeHighlight: const filter = { status: params.get('status') ?? 'open' }; // V8 heap @0x7f1a04

steps.label: 2. Bidirectional URL-State Sync Desynchronizes Closures (t = 14 ms)
steps.description: The effect writes setFilterState(filter) and updates URLSearchParams. Two renders capture stale closures of searchParams and filterState across concurrent commit cycles.

steps.label: 3. Object.is() Fails on Dependency Array (t = 28 ms)
steps.description: During reconciliation, React compares Object.is(@0x7f1a04, @0x7f1b88) and evaluates false even though both objects serialize to { status: "open" }. The effect re-queues unconditionally.

steps.label: 4. Uncancelled Fetches Saturate API & Trigger 429 (t = 420 ms)
steps.description: Without a server-state cache machine or AbortController cleanup, 47 uncancelled GET /api/items?status=open requests stack in flight. The edge rate limiter trips and returns HTTP 429.
steps.codeHighlight: fetch('/api/items?status=' + filter.status); // no cache key, no AbortSignal

steps.label: 5. Fixed: URL Primitive Key + AbortSignal (t = 0..420 ms)
steps.description: Removing mirror state eliminates the render cycle. Deriving a primitive string status = params.get('status') ?? 'open' stabilizes Object.is(), deduplicates the query key, and aborts superseded fetches.
steps.codeHighlight: useEffect(() => { const c = new AbortController(); fetch(url, { signal: c.signal }); return () => c.abort(); }, [status]);
